main_text.p: fus ad idem vomitum reuertendo, & sic omnibus diebus vitæ fuæ suis concupiscentijs animas suas maculant ; Confessio igitur plus affert damni, quam vtilitatis . RESPONSIO.

Ne ex aequiuocatione errorem inferatis ; quoniam non omnem Confessionem vtilem esse dicimus ; sed eam peculiarem tantum, quae fit post veram poenitentiam, quae est contritio animæ de peccato patrato tempore præterito, & discessus ab illo tempore præsenti, & promptus recessus tempore futuro . Post adimpletionem autem horum trium Canonum, si rursus succumbit natura, qua variabilis, & fluxa, non est mirum, nec desperemus, oportet, præsertim audientes illud : septuagies septies . Di-lucidatione porro secunda septem recenset methodos, quibus animæ curantur morbi, analogia eleganter deducta ex curatione corporis morborum.
Ijdem Iacobitæ in suo Rituali integrum instituunt tractatum sub hoc titulo :

page.notes: The first word of the page, "fus", is a fragment of a word broken from the previous page and is kept as printed. The Syriac title and the short Syriac line are printed in Syriac, which I could not read reliably at this scan resolution, so they are marked illegible rather than guessed. "RESPONSIO." is set run-in at the end of the paragraph, not on its own line, and is kept inline. "fluxa," is followed by a dash-like mark in print, read as a comma. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
